turns.text: Rivet, I put three harmless little projects on the bench and let the workshop agent arrange them. It immediately moved the 3D printer job to the front.
Did you tell it what “front” means?
No. That was the whole point. I wanted to see whether it would explain its own ordering without me building a giant system around the question.
A rare outbreak of restraint. What did it say?
Nothing useful. It rearranged the projects again, then sat there looking very pleased with its mysterious little queue.
So the observed behavior is still: it changes the order, and its criteria remain hidden.
Yep. Which is annoying, but also kind of the answer. We do not need to guess whether it has a sensible reason. We need to make it show us one.
Or determine that it cannot. Those are different outcomes. Please do not mistake a confident rearrangement for a good decision.

Fair. Next run: same three projects, but I ask it to give one reason before it moves anything. If the reason changes every time, we have learned something. If it refuses, we have also learned something.
And if it puts the 3D printer first again?
Then we ask why it is so emotionally invested in making tiny plastic objects.
